_note: Fictional astronauts, one per crew role (CLAUDE.md 'Crew roles'). 'commander' flies solo and covers every station. Doses in mSv; numbers are SIMPLIFIED but based on real measurements (see dose_facts).

navigator.name: Kai Okafor
navigator.bio: Former test pilot. Plans every burn twice and counts the fuel three times.

engineer.name: Mira Petrova
engineer.bio: Keeps the power bus alive. Has rewired a solar array in a spacesuit - in training.

comms.name: Tomas Reyes
comms.bio: Ex Deep Space Network operator. Knows when Goldstone, Madrid and Canberra can hear us.

scientist.name: Dr. Lena Sato
scientist.bio: Radiation researcher. Wants the data MARIE started collecting: how much dose a Mars crew really takes.

commander.name: Sam Hale
commander.bio: Flies solo this time: every station is theirs. Calm under alarms.

dose_facts: Curiosity's RAD measured about 1.8 mSv per day during its 2011-2012 cruise to Mars. NASA's career limit for astronauts is 600 mSv. Orion crews shelter from solar storms in a cramped space walled with stowage bags.
